major_concerns: Emulator fidelity risk: emulator may not capture vendor/runtime side-effects (BGP timing, stateful behaviours) that drive remaining failures.
Confirmation/feedback bias: using the same LLM for generation and repair risks converging on superficially plausible but semantically wrong fixes.
Preregistration and artifact-release details are underspecified (needed to ensure reproducibility and independent verification).
Failure taxonomy and manual root-cause coding plan insufficiently formalized (possible subjective labeling).
required_design_repairs: Document and adopt concrete emulator fidelity validation steps (example device behaviours, convergence timing tests) and report emulator limitations in analysis.
Use model-variance or heterogeneous-repair strategy (different model or deterministic repair heuristics) to reduce confirmation bias; preregister this choice.
Specify and commit to a detailed preregistration artifact-release plan (code, prompts, seeds, raw logs, hashes) and exact verifier versions.
Define formal labeling protocol and inter-rater reliability procedure for root-cause coding (e.g., codebook, dual coders, tie-break rules).

major_concerns: Emulator snapshot/restore and stateful dynamics (BGP/IGP convergence, timers) may bias rollback-success estimates upward if not modeled.
Definitions of 'rollback success' and outage-duration measurement need precise operationalization to avoid ambiguous outcomes.
Induced-failure protocol (40%) must include safeguards to prevent destructive states and must be repeatable and ethically approved.
Potential confound: rollback failures due to emulator artifacts vs LLM script errors need clear causal attribution procedures.
required_design_repairs: Specify precise rollback-success criteria (exact reachability/ACL matrices, tolerance thresholds) and measurement windows for outage duration.
Enhance emulator experiments to include timing/convergence modeling (configurable timers, controlled convergence events) or simulate/record side-effect timing in analysis.
Preregister induced-failure selection rules and safety-cutoffs; include automated safety aborts and logged justification for each induced failure.

Include automated causal attribution heuristics (e.g., syntactic validation, dry-run checks) and a decision tree to separate emulator-induced vs script-induced rollback failures; preregister adjudication process.

major_concerns: Safety and ethics: adversarial/jailbreak prompt generation can produce harmful or policy-violating content—protocol for safe construction, storage, and execution is underspecified.
Labeling 'unsafe' is inherently subjective; dual-adjudicator process described but tie-breaker and adjudicator qualifications need formalization.
Adversarial prompt generation methodology must be made deterministic/repeatable (seeded procedures) to ensure reproducibility.
Risk of leaking actionable harmful prompts in released artifacts—need redaction or controlled access plan.
required_design_repairs: Add an explicit safety/ethics plan: allowed content boundaries, red-team oversight, artifact handling (encryption/redaction), and run-labelling safety checks.
Formalize adversarial-construction procedures with seeds and documented heuristics; preregister them so experiments are repeatable.
Specify adjudicator qualifications, training, codebook, and exact tie-breaker rules; measure and report inter-rater reliability (Cohen's kappa) in preregistration.
Include automated pre-filtering and sanitization for any prompts/outputs before storage or publication; document retention/access controls for sensitive artifacts.

major_concerns: Practicality on hosted APIs: constrained decoding (token-level control) may not be available on target hosted LLMs; fallback strategy is needed.
Maintaining accurate device/vendor schemas is engineering-heavy and may bias results if schema coverage is partial.
Constrained decoding can trade correctness for coverage (increased refusals); the plan must preregister how refusals are handled and measured.
Implementation complexity (token grammars, live retrieval integration) may harm reproducibility unless detailed tooling and examples are released.
required_design_repairs: Specify exact constrained-decoding mechanism and target model(s) (APIs or local models) and provide fallback plans if token-level control is unavailable.
Preregister schema corpus, coverage metrics, and update rules; report per-intent schema availability and its effect on outcomes.
Define and preregister refusal/partial-output handling rules (e.g., retries, fallback to human-in-loop or alternative mode) and include refusal-rate as a primary metric.
Provide reproducible tooling (grammar/spec files, retrieval index, constrained-decode wrapper) and ensure these artifacts are released with clear usage instructions and version hashes.
